properties.description:
⭐ THE FINDING IS NOT 'SOMEBODY FORGOT TO ADD THE GATE'. It is that the thing the gate checks CANNOT EXIST IN CI. `check_kit_manifest` compares an INSTALLED kit against the kit SOURCE; CI checks out a repository that has never been installed into. There is no manifest to be stale.

═══ AND THE CASE THAT COULD RUN THERE IS ALREADY COVERED ═══

A fresh install DOES happen in CI: `tools/test_init.py` (100 tests, already a CI job) installs into a temp project and asserts *"manifest and file agreeing, as they would after a clean install"*. So pointing the gate at a temp install would be redundant, and pointing it at the repo root would be red. Neither is a gate worth having.

═══ ⚠️ WHY THE ATTEMPT IS WORTH RECORDING RATHER THAN QUIETLY UNDONE ═══

The gate was added on the user's word, and the reasoning behind that word was sound: the check existed, it FAILED on a clean tree (kit 0.30.0 against a 0.41.0 source, plus three shipped command files the manifest did not record), and it ran nowhere. Everything about that was true. What neither of us had checked was whether CI has an installation to check — and it does not.

🛑 SO THE `INVALIDATES` DRAWN AGAINST THAT FACT WAS WRONG AND WAS DELETED. For about twenty minutes the graph asserted the finding was closed at the cause. It is not closed; it is SHARPENED, and the sharpening makes it harder rather than easier to fix.

═══ ⭐ WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY REACH IT, NOT BUILT, NOT ASKED FOR ═══

The server already holds both halves. It writes `reflow2_version` into `<graph>.client.json` at every handshake, and `.reflow2/kit-version.json` sits in the same directory. Comparing them and saying so — the way `served_by.stale` already says the binary was replaced — would reach the DEVELOPER and the FIELD without CI having anything to do with it. That is where the 2026-08-27 reporter's four-source cross-check would have collapsed to one line. Recorded as a candidate in `dec:idea-what-makes-a-field-report-owed`'s neighbourhood, not proposed here.

═══ ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ═══

- **The manifest drift itself WAS cleared**, and that part stands: installer re-run, `.reflow2/kit-version.json` read back from disk as 0.41.0 / d3cb4ab / 36 files, `check_kit_manifest` exit 0. That was a real local fix and is not undone by this.
- **It says nothing about whether a gate SHOULD exist**, only that CI is the wrong place for this one. A local pre-push hook, or the server-side comparison above, are both untried.
- **One repository, one CI configuration.** A project that COMMITS its `.reflow2/` would have a manifest in CI and the gate would work there — reflow2's own choice to gitignore it is what makes this structural here.
properties.name: SHARPENS why kit drift is invisible to CI, and it is STRUCTURAL: CI is never installed into, so the check exits 2 there — the gate was added, measured, and REVERTED
properties.statement: MEASURED 2026-08-28 while trying to close `fact:defect-kit-manifest-drift-is-invisible-to-ci` by adding `tools/check_kit_manifest.py` to `ci.yml` and to AGENTS.md's pre-push block. IT CANNOT WORK. `.reflow2/` is gitignored and NOTHING under it is tracked — `git ls-files .reflow2/` returns zero — so a CI checkout has no installation at all. Run against such a tree the check reports 'nothing installed here' and exits 2, which would turn every build red. Both edits were reverted.
